class: A protection written into the page but never enforced
symptom: Every dashboard form carried a csrf_token field whose value was empty and was never checked, so any website open in the owner's browser could post to 127.0.0.1:5000 (start an application, change saved answers, delete one), and a site that resolves its own name to 127.0.0.1 could read the dashboard.
root_cause: The templates were written with a csrf_token field, as if a framework filled and checked it; Flask does neither on its own, and nothing supplied or verified it. Nothing checked the Host a request was addressed to.
why_tests_missed: The dashboard tests posted forms without any token and passed, which is exactly the hole; none posted from another origin or under another host name.
fix: web_guard.install(): a token made fresh at start-up is put in every page (context processor) and required on every POST, a POST whose Origin or Referer is another site is refused, and a request addressed to any name but 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] is refused. The setup, profile and answers forms carry the token.
prevention: A security control is done only when a test shows it refusing the attack it exists for; a field in a template is not a control.
